name: Wehrmacht
desc: Combined-arms Wehrmacht of 1944: superb optics and long-range guns, but few vehicles built at great cost. Tech slots hold Luftwaffe jets and wonder weapons; the nuclear slots are what-ifs, as Germany never built a bomb.

blitzkrieg.name: Blitzkrieg
blitzkrieg.desc: Fast armor and Stukas hit before you can dig in. Starts with a panzer spearhead.

westwall.name: Westwall
westwall.desc: Concrete, flak and 88s. Starts with a fortified front line.

wunderwaffen.name: Wunderwaffen
wunderwaffen.desc: Rockets and experimental superweapons, built cheap and fired often.

rifleman.name: Kar98k Schuetze
rifleman.desc: Standard German infantry rifle: accurate and sturdy, but its five-round bolt action fires slowly compared with later self-loaders.

assault.name: StG 44 Sturmmann
assault.desc: First mass-produced assault rifle. Intermediate cartridge gives SMG handling with rifle range; arrived too late and in too small numbers.

bazooka.name: Panzerschreck Team
bazooka.desc: 88 mm reloadable rocket launcher with a shaped-charge warhead, copied from the US bazooka. Short effective range and a back-blast.

manpads.name: MG 34 AA Gunner
manpads.desc: MG 34 on a tripod in the air-defence role. Can pester low-flying aircraft but cannot stop armored ground-attack planes.

mg_gunner.name: MG 42 Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: Fires 1,200 rounds per minute with a characteristic tearing sound; the pattern for modern GPMGs.

grenadier.name: Sturmpionier
grenadier.desc: Stick grenades, satchel charges and flamethrower training for clearing bunkers and trenches.

sniper.name: Kar98k ZF39 Scharfschuetze
sniper.desc: Kar98k with 1.5x ZF39 scope, selected for accuracy. Kills at 600 m but is slow to fire.

flamer.name: Flammenwerfer 41
flamer.desc: Man-portable flamethrower with 7 L of fuel and 25-35 m range for about 10 seconds. Terrifying vs bunkers, lethal to carry.

medic.name: Sanitaeter
medic.desc: Unarmed medic with a bag of dressings and morphine; red cross armband is not always respected.

engineer.name: Pionier
engineer.desc: Builds bridges, clears mines and demolishes obstacles; also fights as infantry when needed.

commando.name: Fallschirmjaeger FG 42
commando.desc: Luftwaffe paratroopers armed with the FG 42 automatic rifle. Elite training, but few survive Crete-style losses.

jeep.name: Kuebelwagen
jeep.desc: VW Type 82 with air-cooled flat-four; light, simple and cheap. Unarmored and only lightly armed.

armored_car.name: Sd.Kfz. 234/2 Puma
armored_car.desc: Eight-wheeled reconnaissance car with a 50 mm KwK 39/1, one of the best of the war. Fast and quiet but thinly armored.

apc.name: Sd.Kfz. 251 Hanomag
apc.desc: Carries ten grenadiers with a front MG 34 and rear MG 42. Open-topped, so vulnerable to artillery airbursts.

light_tank.name: Panzer III Ausf. N
light_tank.desc: Reworked Panzer III with a short 75 mm gun for infantry support; outclassed but numerous.

tank.name: Panzer IV Ausf. H
tank.desc: Reliable workhorse with a long 75 mm KwK 40 gun and Schuerzen skirts. Outgunned by the T-34-85 and IS-2 but widely produced.

heavy_tank.name: Tiger II (Koenigstiger)
heavy_tank.desc: 68-ton tank with a 88 mm KwK 43 L/71 and 150 mm sloped front armor. Nearly impenetrable from the front, short on range and fuel.

mammoth.name: Panzer VIII Maus
mammoth.desc: 188-ton prototype with a 128 mm KwK 44 and 200 mm front armor. Only two were built; the engine could not move it fast.

tank_destroyer.name: Jagdpanther
tank_destroyer.desc: Panther chassis with 8.8 cm PaK 43 L/71 in a fixed casemate. One of the best anti-tank vehicles of the war.

flame_tank.name: Flammpanzer III
flame_tank.desc: Panzer III with a Flammenwerfer in the turret. Short range but destroys bunkers and infantry in cover.

artillery.name: Wespe SPG
artillery.desc: 10.5 cm leFH 18/2 gun on a Panzer II chassis. Thin armor but mobile enough to keep up with panzer units.

howitzer.name: Hummel (15 cm sFH 18)
howitzer.desc: 15 cm heavy field howitzer on a Panzer III/IV chassis; one of the strongest mobile artillery pieces.

mlrs.name: Panzerwerfer 42 Maultier
mlrs.desc: Ten-barrel 15 cm rocket launcher on a half-track; fires in seconds and then relocates.

aa_truck.name: Wirbelwind Flakpanzer
aa_truck.desc: Panzer IV hull with a quad 20 mm Flakvierling in an open turret. Highly effective against low aircraft and infantry.

sam_truck.name: Sd.Kfz. 7 8.8 cm Flak
sam_truck.desc: The famous 88 mounted on a half-track; fires at altitudes up to 8,000 m and doubles as anti-tank gun.

repair_vehicle.name: Bergepanther ARV
repair_vehicle.desc: Panther chassis with a winch and crane; recovered tanks under fire and returned them to workshops.

drone.name: Mistel S2 Composite
drone.desc: Obsolete Ju 88 loaded with a 3.8 t hollow-charge warhead and guided into the target by an Fw 190 mounted on top.

fighter.name: Bf 109 G-6
fighter.desc: Main Luftwaffe fighter with a 20 mm cannon and two MG 131s. Small and agile but short on range.

interceptor_jet.name: Fw 190 A-8
interceptor_jet.desc: Radial-engine fighter with four 20 mm cannons and armor plate; the Sturmbock variant was made to shoot down bombers.

stealth_fighter.name: Me 262 A-1a Schwalbe
stealth_fighter.desc: First operational jet fighter, with four 30 mm MK 108 cannons; 150 km/h faster than any Allied fighter. Unreliable engines.

strike_jet.name: Ju 87 G Stuka
strike_jet.desc: Stuka fitted with two 37 mm BK 3.7 cannon; Hans-Ulrich Rudel destroyed over 500 tanks with the type.

helicopter.name: Fl 282 Kolibri
helicopter.desc: Synchropter used for convoy spotting and anti-submarine patrol; only about 24 were built and none carried real firepower.

gunship.name: Hs 129 B-3
gunship.desc: Twin-engine attack plane armoured against small arms; the B-3 carried a 7.5 cm BK 7.5 cannon. About 25 were built.

light_bomber.name: Ju 88 A-4
light_bomber.desc: Fast, versatile twin-engine bomber also used as dive bomber and night fighter.

bomber.name: He 111 H-6
bomber.desc: Glass-nosed twin-engine bomber, vulnerable to fighters after the Battle of Britain.

heavy_bomber.name: He 177 A-5 Greif
heavy_bomber.desc: Four-engine bomber with two coupled engines; the tendency to catch fire limited its usefulness.

stealth_bomber.name: Horten Ho 229
stealth_bomber.desc: Jet flying wing with possible radar-absorbing glue; only prototypes flew. Modelled as a small stealthy bomber.

diver.name: Kampfschwimmer
diver.desc: Naval commandos using limpet mines against bridges and ships; trained late in the war at Venice.

patrol_boat.name: S-100 Schnellboot
patrol_boat.desc: Diesel-powered S-boats dashed at 40 knots to hit coastal convoys with torpedoes and 20 mm guns.

gunboat.name: Siebel Ferry Gunboat
gunboat.desc: Catamaran ferry fitted with 88 mm guns and flak; invasion barge converted to river and coastal defence.

missile_boat.name: T-24 Torpedoboot
missile_boat.desc: Type 39 torpedo boat with four 10.5 cm guns and six torpedo tubes; larger than a destroyer escort.

destroyer.name: Z-31 (Zerstoerer 1936A)
destroyer.desc: Large 3,000-ton destroyer with five 15 cm guns, ill-suited to rough seas. Fast but short-ranged.

cruiser.name: Admiral Hipper
cruiser.desc: Eight 20.3 cm guns, 14,000 t. Bold raider with poor reliability from high-pressure steam plants.

battleship.name: Bismarck
battleship.desc: Eight 38 cm guns and heavy armor. Sank HMS Hood in 1941 before being hunted down; the Kriegsmarine's only real peer to the Allies.

submarine.name: U-boat Type XXI
submarine.desc: Streamlined with huge batteries; 17 knots submerged. Revolutionised submarine design but entered service in 1945.

aircraft_carrier.name: Graf Zeppelin
aircraft_carrier.desc: Launched in 1938 but never completed; planned for 40 aircraft. In game it carries a mixed, slow-cycling air group.

mg_turret.name: MG 42 Nest
mg_turret.desc: Stellung with MG 42 and interlocking arcs of fire; a few well-sited guns can halt a battalion.

pillbox.name: Westwall Regelbau
pillbox.desc: Standard design from the Siegfried Line: reinforced concrete up to 2 m thick, with MG embrasures.

at_gun.name: PaK 40 7.5 cm
at_gun.desc: Excellent 75 mm gun that could defeat most Allied tanks at 1,000 m; heavy to relocate.

cannon_turret.name: Panther-Turm Stellung
cannon_turret.desc: Panther turret set on a concrete base; used on the Atlantic Wall and in Italy as a cheap, well-armored gun.

mortar_pit.name: GrW 34 8 cm Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: Standard German 81 mm mortar with 2,400 m range; high rate of fire for its time.

flak_battery.name: 3.7 cm Flak 36/37
flak_battery.desc: Automatic 37 mm gun; reasonable against low aircraft but short-ranged.

sam_site.name: 8.8 cm Flak 36/37
sam_site.desc: The 88: 8.8 cm shells up to 10 km. Excellent against aircraft and tanks alike.

heavy_battery.name: Batterie Todt 38 cm
heavy_battery.desc: Four 38 cm SK C/34 guns from the Atlantic Wall; capable of striking targets across the Channel.

railgun.name: 80 cm Schwerer Gustav
railgun.desc: Largest-calibre gun ever used in combat: 80 cm, shell 7.1 t. Only two built; used at Sevastopol 1942.

ciws.name: Flakvierling 38
ciws.desc: Four 20 mm Flak 38 on one mount; 1,800 rpm for a hail of fire against low aircraft.

interceptor_battery.name: Wasserfall SAM
interceptor_battery.desc: Radio-guided liquid-fuel SAM; 35 flight tests but never fielded. Modelled as the Reich's missile screen.

abm_battery.name: Enzian SAM Battery
abm_battery.desc: Me 163-derived rocket-powered SAM. A paper project; no German system could actually hit a ballistic missile.

barricade.name: Tschechenigel Hedgehog
barricade.desc: Welded steel beams that stop tanks; used on beaches and in streets.

repair_depot.name: Feldwerkstatt
repair_depot.desc: Mobile Kfz workshop that repairs vehicles and weapons close behind the front.

coastal_battery.name: 15 cm Kuestenbatterie
coastal_battery.desc: 15 cm TbK C/36 guns in open casemates for the Atlantic Wall; 22 km range vs ships.

tactical_missile.name: Rheinbote
tactical_missile.desc: Four-stage solid rocket with a 40 kg warhead; 160 km range but poor accuracy. Used against Antwerp in 1944-45.

cruise_missile.name: Fi 103 (V-1)
cruise_missile.desc: Pulse-jet cruise missile with a 850 kg warhead; 250 km range, shot down by fighters and flak.

cluster_missile.name: 15 cm Nebelwerfer Salvo
cluster_missile.desc: Barrage of six-barrel Nebelwerfers; saturates a zone with HE.

bunker_buster.name: PC 1400 X (Fritz X)
bunker_buster.desc: Radio-controlled armor-piercing bomb that sank the battleship Roma in 1943; the first precision guided munition used in combat.

ballistic_missile.name: A4 (V-2)
ballistic_missile.desc: First long-range ballistic missile; 1 t of amatol and 320 km range. Nothing could stop it.

hypersonic.name: A9/A10 Amerika-Rakete
hypersonic.desc: Paper project for a two-stage rocket to reach New York; never built.

tactical_nuke.name: Uranbombe (what-if)
tactical_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. The wartime Uranverein never got beyond experimental reactors.

nuke.name: A10 Uran-Rakete (what-if)
nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Modelled as a V-2 follow-on carrying an atomic payload.

mega_nuke.name: Wunderwaffe Zero (what-if)
mega_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Pure fiction; included to keep the match balanced.
